task_id.description: hash key; opaque slug or uuid

sk.description: range key. "HEADER" = the task's current state (one per task; every GSI + hot read lives here); "<ms>#<id>" = an append-only changelog row (who changed which field, from -> to) written on every header update

content.description: free-form text describing the task. PUBLIC BY CONSTRUCTION: this field is a TEMPLATE — `$1`/`$2` stand where a firm-specific value goes and the values ride `private_values`. A public issue files from this field verbatim, so a writer that puts a name here breaks the contract rather than tripping a filter

private_values.description: for a task whose `content` is a TEMPLATE (an escalation), the values its $1/$2 placeholders stand for, in order. Never published — the template is what a public issue is filed from, and keeping the values in a separate secret field is what makes that filing safe by construction rather than by the filer remembering to strip them

contact_id.description: FK into modules/contacts/ when this task is about a contact

journal_entry_id.description: FK into the accounting ledger when this task annotates a journal entry

purchase_order_id.description: FK into modules/purchasing/ (future) when this task is about a PO

invoice_id.description: FK into modules/invoicing/ (future) when this task is about an invoice

subject_key.description: FK to an asset (`1#walk-in-fridge`) or inventory item the task is ABOUT — incidents and maintenance attach here; service history is the query by this key. an asset or item — a thing, not a party

parents.description: task_ids this task is a child of — a subtask names one parent, several make a DAG (one fix serving two issues; an incident attaching to its class). Children of X = the open set filtered by contains(parents, X); an open child blocks the parent's delivery

category.description: work/failure category (e.g. refrigeration, plumbing, pos) — the future incident-signature dimension

assigned_to.description: the agent identity this task is handed to ("agent" = this gerp's own). A change to this field pokes the assignee — assignment IS the handoff. an agent identity or gerp_id, not a private person

due_date.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) or ISO datetime — the CEILING (when this must ship; a stamped commitment when one exists). Past = overdue. Distinct from quote (the moving forecast)

quote.description: the CURRENT delivery quote (forecast) — re-quoted as the queue shifts; history lives in the changelog rows. due_date is the ceiling a commitment stamps; quote is when it's actually expected to ship

delivery.description: when the work actually shipped. Set ONCE by a conditional write (the ratchet — first close wins) which also removes open_flag. Absent = open. Supersedes the old resolved_at

open_flag.description: lambda-managed sparse-GSI partition. Set to "1" while delivery is absent; REMOVE'd by the delivery ratchet. Not user-settable

investigated_by.description: who worked an `alarm` task: `local` (a person with a Claude session, scripts/investigate.sh), a gerp_id (that gerp's agent from its poke), or a managed investigator's name. Several investigators may work one task; each names itself

finding.description: what the investigator read: the lines, the metric, the queue's head — the evidence, quoted, not the judgment

root_cause.description: the investigator's judgment of why, one paragraph, naming the code, the config row or the dependency

proposed_fix.description: what to change and where; a fix that is code is a push after a person's review, a redrive is the queue's redrive, a rule is the owner's on their gerp
